title: Introduce sequence-coherence regression limiter and CI traffic shepherd hook
author: Maya Chen
release_notes:
- Adds a sequence-coherence delta scorer to detect regressions that only appear across multi-turn contexts.
- Introduces a CI hook (traffic-shepherd) that rate-limits rollout traffic to new model variants when coherence degradation is detected.
- Default behavior: soft-fail CI (block merge only after 3 consecutive flagged runs) to reduce noisy interrupts.
description:
Context and motivation:
We observed intermittent regressions where single-turn metrics (e.g. per-turn BLEU/EM) passed, but multi-turn sequence coherence dropped for a small subset of prompt-sets used in chat flows. These failures are often noisy and surface only at scale, leading to slow rollbacks or undetected user-impacting regressions. ENG-8124 asked for a narrow, low-friction mechanism to: 1) detect sequence-level coherence regressions, 2) surface those in CI with an actionable signal, and 3) avoid noisy hard-blocks during early detection.

What this PR does (summary):
- Adds a new scorer pipeline module: seq_coherence_delta. The scorer computes a cohesion score by aggregating turn-level semantic similarity and discourse-level entailment signals across multi-turn prompt samples. The output is a normalized delta vs baseline and a per-cohort severity tag.
- Adds CI hook: traffic-shepherd. The hook runs lightweight shadowed evaluation on a sampled traffic window and, on repeated flagging, reduces promotion rate for the head branch (canary-style traffic cap) rather than outright failing the pipeline.
- Plumbs the scorer into the eval orchestration: a new evaluation task type (seq-coherence-check) and an optional config flag in eval-configs to opt a prompt-set into sequence-aware checks.
- Adds test coverage and a small synthetic prompt-set generator for deterministic unit tests.

Implementation notes and trade-offs:
- The seq_coherence_delta scorer is intentionally conservative: it prioritizes precision over recall to keep false positives low. Score thresholds are configurable per-cohort and stored as metadata in the prompt-set manifest.
- The traffic-shepherd hook implements a 3-run grace window: only after 3 consecutive CI runs with severity >= medium does it escalate to a hard-fail block. This reduces churn from flakey signals.
- We avoided adding heavy external dependencies; the discourse entailment model is a distilled transformer baked into the eval-harness artifacts and quantized to keep CI runtime modest.

Review conversation (selected highlights):
- Alejandro Ruiz (review): "Nice signal design. I worry about threshold drift over time; can we add an automated monthly calibration job?"
  - Maya: "Added a follow-up ticket (ENG-9970) and wired a calibration flag into the scorer. We'll follow up with a background calibration cron job in a later PR to keep this change reviewable."
- Priya Das (review): "The 3-run grace window is reasonable. Please document how ops will be notified when the hook starts rate-limiting traffic."
  - Maya: "Added CI annotations and a lightweight webhook payload that posts to the eval-alerts Slack channel. See tests/integration/test_traffic_shepherd.py for payload example."
- Jordan Park (review): "Integration test is flaky on macOS runners; suggest switching to a dockerized-integration job."
  - Maya: "Switched integration job to dockerized runner and reduced external timing dependence. Marked the previous flaky test with xfail in the commit history."

CI and validation:
- Initial CI run: lint ✅, unit tests ✅, integration ❌ (timing flake on the traffic simulation).
- Second run after fix: lint ✅, unit tests ✅, integration ✅.
- Performance note: seq_coherence scorer adds ~1.1s per 20-sample batch in the shadow evaluation path; traffic-shepherd runs only on sampled shadow traffic so overall CI runtime increase is modest.

Backward compatibility and opt-in path:
- By default the seq-coherence checks are opt-in per prompt-set. Existing prompt-sets see no change unless maintainers update their eval-config to enable the new task type.

Follow-ups and roadmap items (linked):
- ENG-9970: monthly threshold calibration job and historical drift dashboard.
- SUP-4123: add onboarding guide for platform users to opt prompt-sets into sequence checks and interpret severity tags.

Merge outcome:
- After approvals from Alejandro and Priya and green CI, PR was squashed and merged to main on 2026-02-18. Release notes added to changelog under Evaluation section.

How to review locally:
1) python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
2) pip install -e .[dev]
3) run unit tests: pytest tests/unit/test_seq_coherence.py
4) run integration (docker): ./ci/run_integration.sh --hook traffic-shepherd

Checklist: 
- [x] Tests added/updated
- [x] Docs updated
- [x] Linear ticket referenced
- [x] No breaking changes by default (opt-in)

If you want a narrower diff for review, consider reviewing commit-by-commit; the bulk of additions are self-contained under eval_harness/scorers and eval_harness/hooks.
